# nova-sprint roadmap

<!-- Generated from docs/roadmap.sexp by tools/roadmap. Do not edit this file: edit docs/roadmap.sexp and run `make roadmap`. -->

This is the nova-sprint, nova-card and nova-work work after the point releases. The release plan (the owner, 2026-10-11) replaces the ladder of 2026-10-09. The v1.2.x point releases come first and are cut in turn: v1.2.10 (being cut), v1.2.11 small fixes, v1.2.12 tests and models only, v1.2.13 contraction (fewer lines, no behaviour change), v1.2.14 the next small fixes; FIXES.md holds each one's scope and fixes, and an item below whose target is a v1.2.x release is waiting for its card. The aim is v1.2.x working pretty well, so it is the reference for intended behaviour: v1.3, unstable, is the re-architecture (the client/server conversion, then each layer secured from the bottom), built by the sprint running on v1.2.x and checked against it, rather than a blind rewrite; like getting a compiler self-hosting, then using it to build a better compiler. v1.4 is the stable release of v1.3, architecturally correct top to bottom. Point releases continue until only architectural items are open: an area stops taking point fixes when a fix there is the same problem in another form, or would be its third, and each v1.3 architectural item names the point fixes it replaces. Friend work is dogfooded within the week, once more friends are online: friends alone, then friends and fleet together, each friend bug a point-release card. These items were the sprint half of nova-tools' roadmap and moved here with the split, with the sprint's docs and models; nova-tools' ROADMAP.md holds the rest. Point-release work is in FIXES.md, not here. Each item says what it is and why it waits. Where the code already has part of an item, the item says what exists and covers only the gap.

## Lessons from Prime Agent's rewrite

Prime Intellect's write-up of rewriting Prime Agent with AI workers (https://www.primeintellect.ai/blog/prime-agent-rust) names what made a large AI-built rewrite hold together. Each item is one of those lessons, checked against nova's code at dev 9ff68178: what already exists is named by file and line, and the item covers the rest.

### The verifier is its own system stage

A card's checks are written before the work starts. After the work, a verifier stage of the system runs them in a fresh bench, apart from the reader, and its verdict is the merge gate: the named test must fail at the card's base and pass at its head, run by the system rather than reported by the worker. This changes the card contract (the TEST line becomes a check the system runs), the lander (one red-at-base, green-at-head run per card before the batch gate) and the reader's job (it reads a change already shown to do what the card says).

Already in the code: The card lint requires the named test to be absent at the base: rule donewhen-test-name, internal/swarm/lintbase.go:198-236 and internal/swarm/lintpaths.go:174-192. The member's native gate runs failing tests at the base only to classify a failure the worker already reported as not done (cmd/nova-swarm/nativegate.go:26-42). The lander's tree gate runs the batch at its head and reads the TEST line only to time the package (internal/sprint/gate_wall.go:46-59). No step runs the named test red at base and green at head as a gate; that is the gap. The system gates before reads item, under the sprint system, holds the cards that started on it.

Why it waits: A new system stage, not a fix.

### The reader is a different model from the implementer

A reader catches more when it does not share the implementer's blind spots. The rule: a card's reads go to a model other than the one that did the work, with an adversarial brief (find what is wrong; do not summarize) and access to the repository at the card's head. This changes read dealing and the read brief, and adds the rule to SPEC-SPRINT.

Already in the code: nova-sprint set --read-tier and stream set --read-tier raise the tier reads draw from (cmd/nova-sprint/verbs.go:3375 and 3469), and a friend never reads her own work (internal/sprint/friend_read.go:333). Nothing requires a different model; that rule is the gap.

Why it waits: A new dealing rule, not a fix.

### Findings go back to the same implementer

A reader's findings go back to the worker that wrote the change, as a rework of the same card: never a new card, and never a fresh worker who has to learn the change again.

Already in the code: This is the rule for cards and friends today. A card is edited in place, never twinned, and a friend's rework comes back to her (ReworkPinned, internal/sprint/friend_deal.go:89-96). The gap is the fleet, where a machine card's rework can go to any member. That is card rework-goes-to-the-same-worker-b, held under the dealing policy item.

Why it waits: Mostly in place; the rest is a dealing policy change, listed once under the dealing policy item.

## The sprint system

New verbs, stages and policies for nova-sprint. Each is new capability, so none of it fits the fixes-only ladder.

### Processor layers 3 to 8

The upper layers of the nova-sprint processor design: cards that name operands outside the sprint, a route predictor run in shadow first, speculative dispatch, vector cards that make one change across many targets, and a spend governor.

Why it waits: New capability; no new features through v1.4.

Replaces 6 open sprint cards, each mapped to `processor-layers`.

### A merge tree for promotion

Promotion through a merge tree: a root, a shadow, and a switch between them; and a stream's batch built from its cards' branches. Its TLA+ model goes with it: the merge-tree half of card tla-merge-tree-promotion-b. The promotion half of that card models shipped code and stays in v1.4.

Why it waits: New capability.

Replaces 4 open sprint cards, each mapped to `merge-tree`.

### Dealing policy

Changes to how work is dealt: subscription-billed friends before paid API, fewer tokens per friend card, a rework back to the same worker on the fleet as well as for friends, shared paths worked in parallel, and deal latency measured and bounded.

Why it waits: A policy change, not a fix.

Replaces 5 open sprint cards, each mapped to `dealing-policy`.

### System gates before reads

Checks the system can make run before any reader is paid: a mechanical card is proved by the system and not read, and the work lint proves that a card's test pins its change. This is where the verifier stage, under the lessons, starts.

Why it waits: New capability.

Replaces 3 open sprint cards, each mapped to `machine-gates-before-reads`.

### Integrity checks (fsck)

Checks the seat or a person can run at any time: each friend's queue agrees with the store, nothing is held without a beat, every pushed head is recorded, the server's runs and pushes agree, and every landed card is on the base.

Why it waits: New verbs.

Replaces 5 open sprint cards, each mapped to `fsck-integrity-verbs`.

### Two new alarms

An alarm when the store's latency passes its bound, and one when a test process is left running on a fleet machine.

Why it waits: New capability.

Replaces 2 open sprint cards, each mapped to `new-alarms`.

### A spend circuit breaker with a budget per tier

Dealing to a tier stops when its spend passes the tier's budget, and says so.

Why it waits: New capability. The per-model request budget the owner named is v1.3 and separate.

Replaces 1 open sprint card, each mapped to `spend-circuit-breaker`.

### Retire the stopgaps once their verbs exist

Each stopgap goes when the verb that replaces it exists: the bud runners, buswatch, the ping and beat loops, the opencode runners, the coordinator's shell lanes, and the hand steps of promotion.

Why it waits: Each one waits on a new verb.

Replaces 7 open sprint cards, each mapped to `retire-stopgaps`.

### A verb to reland a card from its commits

A verb that lands a card again from named commits.

Why it waits: A new verb.

Replaces 1 open sprint card, each mapped to `reland-from-commits-verb`.

### A cost category for friend work, in tokens

Friend work counted in tokens as its own cost category beside the tiers, so subscription work shows its real size.

Why it waits: New capability.

Replaces 1 open sprint card, each mapped to `friends-token-cost-category`.

### The tree gate tells a bench fault from a red test

When a gate fails because of the bench rather than the code, the lander says so and does not charge the card for it.

Already in the code: Part of it is on dev (c5922306bf, 5d8e164a50); pull request 5476 carries more.

Why it waits: Parked by the owner, 2026-10-09.

Replaces 1 open sprint card, each mapped to `lander-bench-fault-classifier`.

### Refuse a need that names a dropped card, and list dependants on drop

Admission already refuses a need that names no record, but a dropped card is still a record. Add refuses a need on a card that can no longer land, and dropping a card lists the cards that need it.

Target: v1.5

### Convert every client-held copy of sprint state to client/server

The first v1.4 rewrite step. Each item in the 2026-10-10 inventory where a client keeps its own copy of sprint state is converted in place so the server is the one truth and clients ask it: the friend daemon's lanes and epoch, the member loop's lane table and local recovery (one lane protocol for friends and fleet), the seat's file proof, friend messages through folders and the separate bus Redis, config split across Postgres and the store, hosts following versions, the dashboard's own snapshot, and the lander as a second truth in git. All state is keyed by epoch. A TLA+ model of the lane protocol comes first. Faults found while the point releases run are recorded here as input.

Why it waits: Point releases continue meanwhile; their faults are the input to this rewrite cleanup.

Target: v1.5

From: the owner, 2026-10-11

### Secure the sprint's layers from the bottom up

Name the layers that are really there and secure each in turn, lowest first, each an anchor so a later fault stops there: L0 machine (one join entry point, drift check, doctor member-env green); L1 transport (loops re-dial, seat proof, push delivery); L2 providers and routes (the global limiter live, a provider fault never fails a card); L3 deal and take (a machine fault holds the machine, no silent ready); L4 read (no lost verdict, no cannot-ask while readers idle); L5 land (ledger merge done, judgments rare and hands-off); L6 observability (doctor and pushes catch every fault first). A layer is secured when it has a TLA+ model with reversed witnesses checked by TLC, tests on a real store including every refusal, a second reader's probes green, real use by the seat and by friends, docs, and a lock agreed with the owner.

Why it waits: Comes after the client/server conversion of the 2026-10-10 inventory, so the layers are secured on the converted design rather than on client-held state.

Target: v1.5

From: the owner, 2026-10-11

Coordination nodes follow one uniform contract at any depth. The spec's five behaviours get tests that drive a seeded kernel with no model.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #2354

### Hand back launcher refusals and refuse re-dealing a dealt label

A launcher refusal before any process starts returns the card to the queue instead of raising it unknown. The queue remembers dealt labels and refuses a repeat unless forced.

Target: v1.5

From: issue #2381; issue #2382

### System runs the gate and owns returned, verified and landed transitions

Harvest runs the gate itself outside the wall and records the result; a card's own gate claim is data. Returned, verified and landed are recorded transitions per item, head and base, and the landing lane is plain verbs with a model only for exceptions.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #2386; issue #2530; issue #2508; issue #2407

### Mechanical pin-check read for test-only pull requests

A reader reverts the commit each new test claims to pin, expects red, restores it and expects green, and reports per test.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #2387

### Each machine computes its sprint row and pushes it to a store

Every machine builds its own row of queue, working, done, ok, fail and rates every ten seconds, and the viewer reads the store.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #2389

### Cut the per-card cost in setup, tests and parallelism

Self-contained cards need no repo, cards run only the useful test command with cached tool discovery, and Go parallelism is bounded per card.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #2399; issue #2400; issue #2401

### Reviewer findings on the current batch jump to the front

A finding on the current batch becomes a card at the front of the swarm and merge queue, keeping the fix close to the base.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #2417

### Make reads cheap with CI evidence and a short mechanical PR brief

CI carries the machine-checkable evidence and the PR body opens with title, goal, write scope and test command. Report and read start when the PR opens, and the reader sees only the diff and statuses.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #2449; issue #2531; issue #2509

### Escalate a node that fails twice to the next tier

A node that fails the bar twice on a cheap route moves up a tier with both attempts attached, never a third recut at the same tier.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #2450

### Parse typed approve verdicts and release untyped holds

A typed approve line is counted, and an untyped hold can be released by a read.

Target: v1.5

From: issue #2454

### Typed card outputs and resume by content key and deal-time base

Result and read files follow a schema parsed without a model. A finished result is cached by card text and base, and the base is pinned at deal time.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #2506; issue #2507; issue #2529

### Sprint table counts come from a card event stream, not file times or comment scans

Done, ok, fail, read, landed and calibration counts per friend and per bench are folded from card events, so the table needs no GitHub scan and shows cut to landed.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #2563; issue #2678; issue #2680

### Sprint x/y percent and ETA come from the work set

One reader loads the roadmap and work files, a landed acceptance kind exists, and a sprint is any bounded task set answering x/y percent in under a second, with GitHub issues ingested into the file.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #2595; issue #2664; issue #2679; issue #2593; issue #3141

### Opening a sprint stamps its start on every machine

The sprint verb records the start once, and bench counts read it, so counts never include an earlier sprint.

Target: v1.5

From: issue #2727

### Cards carry a stable id, ruling and spec links, and a reverse walk from PR to reason

Each card gets a stable id carried to job, result, event and PR body, names its ruling and spec anchor, and one query answers why a PR exists, with its siblings and attempts.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #2589; issue #2596; issue #2597

### A needs-you line lists what waits on a person, oldest first

The sprint table and status print the items waiting on a human, such as asked cards, PRs with no typed line and held cards, with who is expected, and a supervisor owns the notifications.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #2592

### The merge gate keeps raw test output and full review text, and stores its receipt

The batch test step keeps the raw go test JSON stream, paginated review captures are not truncated at the output cap, and the gate's receipt is stored where a reader can fetch it.

Target: v1.5

From: issue #2626; issue #2654; issue #2693; issue #3183

### GitHub events arrive in a stream so loops are event-driven

A webhook receiver writes GitHub events to a stream with a durable consumer and a polling fallback, so PR, CI and typed-line changes reach loops and the table within seconds.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #2657; issue #2685

### Owner decisions are records with options, default, deadline and ruling

A decide verb opens, shows and rules decision records, and the table shows one count of open decisions.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #3143

### nova-work ingest from GitHub: capture, continuous poll, verify and cutover

nova-work reads issues from GitHub into its own store with conditional requests, keeps in sync from deliveries and a poll, and has a verify run. The tracker becomes a mirror once the cutover is done.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #3167; issue #3169; issue #3172; issue #3173; issue #2080; issue #2081; issue #2082

### nova-work write-back: one writer, roadmap batch, lag and fold of landed work

One writer applies roadmap batches back to the tracker, reports how far the mirror lags, and settles units when landed pull requests and verified criteria arrive.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #3168; issue #3171

### nova-work keeps specs in its store behind a single-writer kernel

Specs, their versions and reader scores live in the nova-work store, and the ready gate is computed from them. One kernel owns the store and every mutating verb is a kernel command.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #3220; issue #3340

### All coordination state in Redis, batched, driven by Go tools

Queues, leases and tables live in the sprint store, not in files. Every store access is a pipelined batch, every loop ticks at one second, and coordination scripts move into Go verbs.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #3279; issue #3303; issue #3309

### Decisions are made centrally; machines only execute what the queue says

A worker machine takes the next ready item, runs it and reports. It never decides readiness from a partial view.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #3251

### The coordinator is a role any friend AI can hold on any machine

Every coordinator action is a verb, and the loops and tables run on any Mac or Linux machine with failover, so no step depends on one person or host.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #3295; issue #3543; issue #2061; issue #2062; issue #2065; issue #2066; issue #2069; issue #509; card moved out of the sprint (work record, 2026-10-04)

### A pit stop and its lift are one store state every friend reads

The stop and its lift are set and cleared by a verb and held in the sprint store, so a friend never relies on a bus note to know whether to work.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #3371

### One verb moves ready work to whoever has open slots

A single atomic verb cancels stale items and moves ready work across queues to friends with open slots, honouring the named owner, instead of hand loops.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #3407

### One DEPENDS-ON form and one parser that refuses other spellings

Cards, pull requests and issues state dependencies in one canonical form read by one parser. Unknown dependency state is never treated as satisfied.

Target: v1.5

From: issue #3409

Spec reads use one machine-checked line form written by a verb. A verb computes the gate verdict from the store, reads are keyed to the body hash so stale ones never count, and a rewrite names the gaps it closes.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #3564; issue #3565; issue #3566; issue #3568; issue #3569

### Merge streams: the stream is the landing unit with open, take, batch, land verbs

A stream is opened, taken, batched, marked and landed as a unit, holding at its boundary. Cancelled or timed-out shards count as red.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #3478

### Show every seat's children on the sprint table within a second

The table shows each live child with task, step, age and cost, read from the store, including reads and spec reviews that hold no queue lease.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #3519

### Bound turns and reasoning on the live card templates

Read-family cards carry a low turn limit and low reasoning, and writing-family cards a higher one, to cut tokens per card.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #3534

### Sprint table: disk room per host and one consumer table for friends and hosts

The sprint table shows free disk per host, red under the floor, and one table shape (ready, working, done, ok, fail, ok%) for friends and hosts.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #3584; issue #4071

### The card record is the only record; GitHub is a remote written at the edges

Cards carry their fields as structured data imported once at creation. Nothing parses prose or edits a pull request body, and GitHub is touched only to close out. A call budget guard counts remaining GitHub calls meanwhile.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #3594; issue #3596; issue #3601; issue #3607; issue #3633; issue #3603; issue #3967

### A read is one record written only by the verb

Reads live in one record with one writer, and a read counts only when the verb writes its score line. A score posted only on the bus cannot exist.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #3874; issue #3897; issue #2063

### Cards carry what changed on the base, and merge notes reach live workers

The card cut lists base commits touching its paths since the issue, and a note verb lets merge learnings reach a worker mid-task.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #4189; issue #4186

### Cards flow automatically through the tables, moved only by single-writer verbs

A waiting card is complete, so a deal is one move. Verbs deal, work, end, land and cancel are the only writers of stream, host and friend sets, and everything stays in the store under one second.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #3636; issue #3662; issue #3911; issue #3929

### The stream table is true end to end; every refusal and failed card is raised

Each column change is an event, a nightly control walks a card through all columns, every refusal and error is raised to the coordinator, and a failed card goes to a typed review verdict.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #3999; issue #4155; issue #4072

Beats, presence and history keys drop their TTLs and length caps in favor of recorded time and reader judgment. A reset verb deletes the sprint state families as admin after a backup.

From: issue #4191

### A card is a spec, refused at push without its fields

A card carries evidence, paths with lines, seams, rules, receipts and keep notes. Push refuses a work card missing them, and requires a stream.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #4313; issue #5494

### A parent card cuts children, waits and stitches

A parent fans out from a plan, depends on its children, takes corrections mid-flight, then reviews and stitches in its second phase.

Target: after v1.4

### Dependencies come from paths, with sentinels per layer

Ready means no live path overlap. Streams follow the file graph, overlap is refused at push, and a sentinel card reviews each layer and across streams.

From: issue #4318; issue #4322; issue #4188; issue #4185; issue #4028

One spelling per concept, one receipt shape, fast quiet calls and a home screen. The system settles what it can before waking the coordinator.

A fresh coordinator seat gets a durable, supervised recipe that turns new judgments and notes into a wake for its harness. Delivery, wake and acknowledgement are separate steps.

Target: after v1.4

Watchdog exit must not wait on diagnostics that can block. A negative deadline is refused.

### Cost rules: flash first, escalate repeats, rest failing routes

Cheap tier first, pro only on escalation. Two identical failures escalate at once. A route that returns no result rests. Rules are kept by reference, each with a unit test.

### Generated ledgers merge without conflict and rework starts at the tip

Two cards that shrink the same ledger conflict by line. Regenerate the ledger at the merged tree, and stage rework from the current head.

From: issue #5408; card from the sprint store (2026-10-10)

A fix-red card kind names its source and test files and its reproducing test, and is accepted only when that test goes green. One card per triaged defect.

### nova-work client must stop waiting after a bound

A work client call without a deadline waits forever on a session that never answers. The spec fixes a default bound and the client enforces it.

Target: v1.5

From: issue #1643

### A card goes from issue to landed with no coordinator hand step

List what remains before accept, routing, reads and landing all run by the system alone, and close each gap.

Target: after v1.4

A coordinator learns what each friend can do now and whether workers share one account limit. Stale advertisements do not count.

Target: after v1.4

### Reprioritize, correct and stop work already dealt

Authenticated control events with scope, update number and priority reach every running descendant, and the sprint can prove each one applied.

Target: after v1.4

The sprint persists the goal, gates, priorities and budget, and recovers from a failed worker, exhausted provider or lost context while the owner is away.

Target: after v1.4

A single dealer with per-member queues stops fast-ping machines from winning every card while slow ones sit idle.

### A down machine must never hang the dealer, sampler or harvest

Every remote call has a timeout and each host is isolated, so a dead machine and stale connection sockets cannot freeze the loops.

Provider capacity is a shared resource. Ceilings, an error-rate watch and automatic spill to the next route keep retries from holding slots.

Target: after v1.4

### Derive a machine's width from measured per-card memory with a controlled ramp

Widths are measured, not guessed, and limits are found by a controlled ramp.

Card generators become verbs that cut from a work spec, a repair or a read, and skip work an open or merged pull request already carries.

One signal with a generation is checked by dealing, launch, harvest and landing before each action, and bad signal states cause no side effect.

The first few cards of a new family run alone, and a machine is checked at loop start, so mass failures show in minutes.

Launched, returned, gate result, pull requests and landed are counted per wave and per model, with live cards and widths by machine, all from records.

Two members sharing a commit are not a conflict. The planner finds stacks by ancestry, not by base ref.

One verb collects returns, applies commits, runs the suite, opens the pull request and records each verdict on its source.

Hold an uncertain reservation and never re-grant it on expiry, reap on lease expiry, and give the executor seam a parent grant, a version-bound result and uncertain-on-disconnect.

From: a Gemini dialog the owner shared, 2026-10-10

### A TLA+ case for the false-positive fix loop

A fix passes its own layer but keeps re-failing a sentinel above it. A TLA+ case couples components to domains: a fix confined to PATHS that never meet the regression's component exhausts its attempt bound and halts. When widened PATHS intersect the component, the fix clears it nondeterministically (it may still fail), and every failure counts toward MaxAttempts: intersection is necessary, not sufficient. Properties: a reachable fix can land (liveness under fairness), and a fix that is never right halts at the bound (safety). Open question: does a merge-queue ejection count toward the card's attempt bound? It extends the attempt-bound models in tla-card-lifecycle-counters-and-waits.

Target: after v1.4

From: a Gemini dialog the owner shared, 2026-10-10

### Coordinator drift: a root brief and two metrics

Every escalation carries the root brief, with a test that holds it. Every card cites a release-scope or fixes item directly, never through its parent card, which closes scope laundering. Drift is measured three ways: the share of newly written cards that cite no item in the release-scope or fixes file (cards carry their release); the Jaccard overlap of non-trivial tokens between a card's brief and its cited scope item, warning below a ratio such as 15%; and the branching ratio, consumer cards per producer card per wave. The blind spots these close are scope laundering, semantic dilution and scope bloat.

Target: after v1.4

From: a Gemini dialog the owner shared, 2026-10-10

### An unhooked friend's jobs are returned only on evidence their child ended

Since PR #499 START honours the STOP receipt the STOPPED friend reconcile writes when it retires a friend's working and read cards (internal/sprint/live.go LiveReturns, friend_return.go). The reconcile fires on seat.Unhooked, which nova-hook unhook sets by command: it is not evidence the friend's session stopped. A friend unhooked after a STOP while her session still works a card lets START pass and the primary be dealt again beside her; her stale finish is refused (the card is off the table, its generation stepped), so two processes can work one primary but neither corrupts it. tla/StopReturn.tla Retire assumes child = 0, which the code does not check on this path. Decide the evidence (a live set that no longer names the job, or an explicit cancel acknowledgement) and write the receipt only on it; extend the model so Retire is enabled only on that evidence, with a reversed witness.

From: issue #3393

### A plan gate before code

A card above a size bound writes a plan first, and a reader reviews the plan before implementation starts. The design agreed with the owner on 2026-10-11 has two levels. Inside a card, working splits into planning, then a plan read, then implementing: the plan is committed to the card's branch as PLAN.md, and implementing is a second take on the same branch, so a one-shot child starts from the file, not from memory; a refused plan is a re-plan take. Above cards, a plan node turns a roadmap entry into cards with their dependencies (its scope, the cards, their DEPENDS lines and a read), feeds a stream, holds the cap of about 10 unadmitted drafts, and is what nova-work later imports as a node. Both levels are modelled in TLA+ with the card machine before either is built.

Why it waits: A new system stage, not a fix.

Target: v1.5

From: Rowan, 2026-10-16, from the overnight fix column

### Selftest, the sims and the unit tests run with routes configured, as in use

A store with no routes configured at all treats every tier as served, and each worker runs its own --model. v1.4.6 fences that shortcut so it applies only to the in-memory twin: the pretend sprint of `nova-sprint selftest`, the help walkthrough, and the twin and play sims. A real store with no routes refuses by name. v1.7 removes the shortcut entirely. The selftest twin, the walkthrough, the sims and the roughly 362 unit tests that rely on an empty route table instead configure routes the way a real sprint does, through the same nova-config route rows or their store equivalent, so the tier is respected everywhere with no special case. DONE-WHEN: the predicate that fences the shortcut is deleted; no code path serves a tier without an enabled route; selftest, the walkthrough and the sims configure routes; the full unit tier and TLC (ReaderTiers) pass; and a test pins that an empty route table refuses on every store kind.

Why it waits: The system should be tested exactly as it will be used. A special case that serves every tier when no routes exist is a path a real sprint never takes, so the tests that rely on it prove less than they appear to, and keeping it, even fenced, leaves a way for the tier rule to be skipped.

Target: v1.7

### Swarm mode: the whole fleet and every friend go wide on one problem

A new mode beside the deal. Instead of many cards to many workers, one hard problem goes to every lane at once: every fleet member's lanes and every friend's width, each attacking the same problem independently. Coordination is shared across the message bus plus a few text files in a repo: a findings log (what each lane learned), a dead-ends list (what failed and why, so no lane repeats it), and a leaderboard of candidate heads with their gate results. The problem's tests, or an outside judge, rank the candidates; the first head that passes every gate wins, or the best one at a deadline. Design questions for the card: diversity across lanes (different models, tiers, prompts and starting points, so lanes are not copies); how much each lane reads of the shared files, and when (sharing too early collapses diversity, too late wastes work); a budget and a stop rule (a token cap, a wall clock, and stopping once a winner lands); merging partial results from several lanes; and fairness of the bus under many writers. It is a state machine (lanes, candidates, judging, stop), so its TLA+ model comes first. Predicated on nova-tools v1.7 rename-nova-swarm-to-nova-worker, which frees the name: this mode is nova-swarm.

Why it waits: Some problems are worth many independent attempts at once: hard bugs, R&D and frontier cards. Today the sprint can only split work, not converge many minds on one problem.

Target: v1.7

From: Glenn, live, 2026-10-16: 'for v1.7 we could add a swarm mode. This is where entire fleet and friends go wide with each lane solving the same problem, with shared coordination across the message bus and some text files in a repo.'

### Composite verbs: one call does each coordinator act, end to end

Learned from Hermes Agent's programmatic tool calling, which collapses a multi-step pipeline into one inference call. Each coordinator act that today takes 3 to 6 verbs, with traps on the way, becomes one deterministic verb that does the whole act and prints only what to act on. Measured on 2026-10-16: (1) stuck: list every card that is not moving but could be, and why: waiting with every need landed, held by a judgment, or merging but not queued. This is today's tools/stuck-cards-review.sh made a verb. (2) refinish-same-head: re-finish a card whose only fault was the bench or the gate, checking first that the head merges onto the base. (3) fix-missing-base: add a recut card's missing REPO or BASE line in any column (return, brief --keep-head, accept). (4) resolve-bound: clear a misclassified attempt bound (release, then an in-place brief with a dated carry line). (5) accept-on-read: record a cold read with its evidence file, choosing --heavy or --read-ok itself. Each verb has --dry-run, refuses by name with the one next command, and is tested on a real store, including every refusal. Glenn, 2026-10-16: skills are non-deterministic, so lessons become deterministic verbs and checks, never prose skills the agent must remember to apply.

Why it waits: Every manual multi-verb act today cost tokens and hit at least one refusal that needed another verb first; one deterministic verb per act removes both.

Target: v1.7

From: Glenn, live, 2026-10-16, on the Hermes Agent review: '#2 is great idea for v1.7' and 'skills are fine, but remember, skills are non-deterministic'

### Every resolved judgment becomes a recorded lesson, and repeated lessons become verbs or checks

Learned from Hermes Agent's skill loop (the agent writes a skill after solving something and improves it with use), but made deterministic. Glenn, 2026-10-16: skills are non-deterministic. The machine records every resolved judgment as data: the judgment kind, the cause the coordinator named, the verbs that fixed it, and how long the card was stuck. When a cause repeats past a threshold, the machine raises a named judgment proposing the fix as code: a composite verb (composite-verbs-one-call-per-coordinator-act), a refusal that names the next command, or a check that stops the cause at its source, so a hulk-style bench fault or a recut card with no BASE line is caught before it strands cards. A lesson never lives only as prose for an agent to remember. Today's examples, to seed it: a bench gate on the wrong Go, a misclassified attempt bound, a recut card missing REPO and BASE lines blocking a whole stream's batch, a false empty-commit on a no-ff merge over a carried head, soft land-after deps on file overlap, and stale GATE-NEEDS judgments after members gained facts.

Why it waits: The coordinator fixed the same few causes by hand many times today; recording them as data and turning repeats into code makes the fix permanent and deterministic.

Target: v1.7

### Card lint locks in the coordinator's lessons: 16 new rules from 30 hours of failed cards

From the coaching analysis of 408 failed events, 2026-10-16 (~/rowan-working/coaching/2026-10-16.md, section 4). 78 events, plus 57 machine PATHS widenings and 156 brief-replaced bounces, were the brief's fault, not the worker's. Each lesson becomes a deterministic rule at add, brief, recut and --widen, refusing with the one next command: L1 generated-outputs-in-paths (needs a per-repo map of which emitter writes which generated files); L2 registry-rows-in-paths (extends paths-cover-registry to make/<lang>.mk, make/negative-controls.json, tablenames, tla CASES/RUNS/RUNS-HISTORY, tools/agentsmap/catalog.go); L3 pinned-digest-in-paths; L4 changed-rule-pins-in-paths (tests and docs that pin the rule being changed); L5 every-brief-names-repo-and-base; L6 needs-are-header-lines-and-live (a named dependency is a DEPENDS-ON or LAND-AFTER line naming a live card); L7 overlap-on-the-table-needs-an-order; L8 donewhen-runs-at-base (every target, script, driver, TLA module, TLC group and sibling exists at BASE or inside PATHS/NEW); L9 siblings-named; L10 host-words-need-gate-needs; L11 staged-job-or-machine-only; L12 roadmap-flip-needs-row-coverage; L13 measure-card-names-its-driver (and refuses a hand-made board); L14 form-has-a-checker (needs a review-checker command); L15 pin-only-to-an-up-friend; L16 tier-floor-by-size (only ever raises a tier). Also from today: BASE must be a stream branch, never another card's branch, since a card that landed onto a card branch never reached its stream (rocketnet-message-objects-and-c-api). Every rule is tested on a real store, including each refusal, and replayed against today's failed cards to show it would have caught them.

Why it waits: Lessons that live in prose are forgotten; skills are non-deterministic (Glenn, same day). A lint rule refuses the bad card before it costs an attempt.

Target: v1.7

### A landing conflict is resolved in the merge step, never a new attempt

When a card's head no longer merges onto its stream's tip, the lander merges the tip into the card's branch, re-runs the card's own gate and lands; only a conflict it cannot resolve, or a gate that goes red after the merge, goes back to the card, and then as a merge task, not a fresh attempt with a new worker and a new read. Today every conflict re-deals the card (fixed-count reached attempt 11 on a two-line make/go.mk conflict).

Target: v1.7

From: the owner, 2026-10-17: these bad merges should not become fixes; they should be done in the merge step

### A route can be marked reads-only

A route can be marked reads-only, so it takes read cards and never work cards. Today a route belongs to one tier and is shared by work and reads (tier set --routes adds it to work dealing too), so a model good for reading but weak at code, such as Ultramarine 1 Flash, cannot be tried on reads alone. Proposal: a reads_only flag on the route row that the work deal skips and the read ask honours, with a route per tier where the tier has none (frontier has no tier row today).

Why it waits: Glenn 2026-10-18: run Ultramarine 1 Flash on reads at every tier; blocker 3 of the trial, no reads-only route placement.

Target: v1.11

THE TASK. R-AUTO-TAKE: "Ready cards for fleet and friend lanes are taken automatically and worked on." A friend with free lanes and ready cards on her row has them TAKEN by the machine, and is told once per take, so she only has to work them. WHY IT FAILS TODAY (measured 2026-10-19 on the live sprint, read these before writing anything): (a) The server never takes for a friend. Every friend deal places the card ready (friend_deal.go:1024 friendDealUnit, createEntry(..., Ready, ...)); the only moves to working are her own start (friend_start.go:74 friendStartUnits, which skips one-shot rows outright at :77-78; her take by id or by lane, steps_work.go takeOne). tla/FriendReadyTake.tla's Tick Fill (the tick filling her free lanes) is not in the code; the module's header says so ("historical abstraction"). For a one-shot row (every live friend row today is mode=one-shot in nova-config) the only taker is the nova-hook lane client in nova-tools (internal/friend/client.go Round), which asks the server lane by lane with a 5 s ask bound inside a 15 s round every 200 s. The server at 127.0.0.1:6390 answered a read friend cards in 0.25 s to over 30 s, and the busiest friend's hook service log (~/.local/state/nova-hook/<name>.log) holds 1382 lane asks and 59 friend-cards asks that missed the bound against 63 rounds that took anything. The row stood at 4 to 12 ready with 9 to 14 lanes free. The client half is the sibling card v17-friend-lane-client-takes-and-renews-in-one-ask (nova-tools); this card makes the server not depend on it. (b) The alarm that should have caught it is dead code: TickDeadlines (steps_tick.go:1781-1785) `continue`s every card on a friend row before friendLaneIdle (steps_tick.go:1792, friend_take.go:270) is read, so FriendReadyMax (friend_take.go:264) never judges a friend's ready card with a free lane. (c) The strict deal at the take (steps_work.go:1703-1716, takeAheadOf) refuses her take by id of a work card while a read or fix ranked above it is takeable ("take <blocker> first"); a friend hit this on 2026-10-19. That refusal is right for a take by id and stays; it is harmless once the machine takes the blocker itself in the same tick. THE CHANGE. (1) The take is the tick's. In friendDealPass, after the start receipts and the deal, for each friend row that is up, hooked (R-HOOKED: friendDealable's worker evidence) and not held, take her ready cards by count into her free room, exactly as takeOne by count does for her today: the same guards (row width from nova-config only, half slots for reads while read cards are on, the card's live generation, needs landed, route rest, provider concurrency budget), in the one order friendDealtOrder gives (reads, then blocker, critical, fix, then work by rank and stream turns). Stamp each card as her lane take does (laneSet: a free lane number from 1 to her width, lane_at now, holder, and her start, FieldStarted at its generation via friendStartSet), so friendUnstartedWorking never bounces it back ready, her lane client finds it held and renews it, and laneGoneUnits returns it only when her lane lease lapses. Batch and one-shot rows alike. A row at width takes nothing more; a down, unhooked or held row takes nothing. (2) Strict order never idles a lane. A card ranked first that cannot be taken now (needs not landed, provider budget, route rest, or a work card needing two half slots where one is free) is passed over for the next card that can; free lanes never idle behind one card she cannot take. A blocker she can take is taken first. The by-id refusal in (c) is unchanged. (3) One notice per tick (coordinator 10-19: batched, message a friend only to act). After the tick's plan commits, the server sends ONE bus message to the friend's own name listing every card it moved into working on her row this tick (the tick's take, a lane take, a take by id): subject `SPRINT CARD TAKEN <card>@<gen> lane=<n> as=friend.<name>`, body naming the card, generation, kind, tier, stream, the brief path the friend reads (`nova-sprint card <card> --brief`, and the job directory when friend sync wrote one), and the finish verb line with her epoch. Use the one push path that exists (coordinator_push.go, bus_envelope.go); a second path is a defect. A card dealt and taken in the same tick gets only the take notice. A notice is sent once per (card, generation, lane): a retried send after a failed bus write is the same message id, never a second notice. The take's answer (the LANE line of take --lane) gains the fact `notice=sent` so a lane client can stop sending its own notice for that hold. (4) The coordinator's alarm. `where` (cmd/nova-sprint/reads.go, the header lines above the work table, and --json) prints one line per friend row that has held a ready card for more than FriendReadyAlarm (a constant, 2 minutes) while she had a free lane: `alarm: friend <name> <k> ready with <n> lanes free for <duration> (oldest <card>)`. And TickDeadlines' friend skip at steps_tick.go:1781-1785 is narrowed so friendLaneIdle's FriendReadyMax judgment fires for a friend's ready card with a free lane (her deadline redeal for working cards stays as it is), one judgment per card, retired when the card is taken or leaves her row. (5) The model. Extend tla/FriendReadyTake.tla (and MCFriendReadyTake): make Tick's Fill the take this card writes (by count, guards abstracted as a per-card Takeable flag, lanes and widths as now), add a per-take notice record, and the invariants LiveRowWithFreeWidthHoldsNoReadyCardPastOneTick (a live, hooked, unheld row with a free lane holds no takeable ready card past one Tick), NoIdleBehindBlocker (no free lane while a takeable card is ready, whatever the rank of an untakeable card ahead of it), EveryTakeAnnouncedOnce (each take into working on her row has exactly one notice), keeping every existing invariant. Batched per tick; through the existing coordinator push path. Tests over a fake bus, clock 1000.0, one per class, each failing if the push is missing or repeated on a tick where nothing changed. THE PIN RULE. Read standard/pins/s9.tsv: its divergence rows naming this card (sprint-spec-fix-push-on-judgment) name the owed tests. Write each owed test first (red at BASE), make it pass, and in the same commit change each such divergence row to a test pin. The checker (internal/ci/standard_pins_test.go) fails a divergence whose owed test exists, so the pin is in place from this card's first commit. Owed tests named in this brief that the row names differently: use the row's name and say so in the report. Read the files START names and the parts of docs/SPEC-SPRINT.md this card names before writing anything. STEP 3. Write the owed tests first, each opening with t.Parallel(); run them at BASE and keep the failing lines. STEP 4. Make them pass in the PATHS and NEW files only. STEP 5. Change the divergence rows to test pins (THE PIN RULE) and run go test -count=1 -timeout 600s ./internal/ci/ -run TestTheStandard. STEP 6. Cold read: spawn one reader with no memory of your reasoning to read the diff against this brief and name any gap as file:line; fix it. STEP 7. Check every other caller or emitter of what changed is handled. STEP 8. Run the gate: go test -count=1 -timeout 900s ./internal/sprint/ ./cmd/nova-sprint/ ./internal/ci/. Read the last line of each. When a test fails, name its file and say whether that file was changed by your work (yours) or is unchanged (already red at BASE: run the same test on the unchanged base to say so), and report that line first. STEP 9. RULES. Work only in the job directory this card names. Never force-push or rebase a shared branch. Never kill a process you did not start. Never start a server on this machine. No `rm -rf` outside the job directory. Report what was not done. Never search /, ~ or /Volumes; search only inside the job's checkout. A test that needs the real thing is a functional test and keeps to that tier. Make the smallest change, with no refactor. Never delete live code for looking unused. Glenn, 2026-10-18: merges and landings run in parallel; only pushes to the SAME base branch are ordered. Distinct bases gate and merge concurrently, without chaining; gates for different base commits run at once; landGrace is not a cross-stream wait; the land width is set from bench capacity, not a fixed 4; the --land-parallel flag cannot go below 2, or is removed. The hard row is `s6:R-LAND-PARALLEL` in the sprint spec (standard/sprint/s6.md, written by sprint-spec-s6-landing; its pins are standard/pins/s6.tsv). A cold read of the spec found landing serializes far beyond pushes to one base: (a) each lane's cuts chain on the prior cut (cmd/nova-sprint/landpass.go, landLane.prior, launch); (b) one base commit's gate is single-writer (landShared.baseGates, baseGate, acquireGate); (c) a batch waits up to landGrace for a higher-priority stream still merging (landpass.go landGrace, graceClock, runLane); (d) the width is capped at 4 (landParallelDefault) so a fifth stream waits, and the fleet's units run `--land-parallel 2`; (e) `--land-parallel 1` merges streams serially (land.go, the flag and its `< 1` check). READ THE CODE FIRST and say in the report which of (a) to (e) really serializes distinct bases at BASE (a lane is already keyed by (clone, base), so some of these may already hold): your tests are red at BASE where it serializes and pin today's behaviour where it does not. Libraries considered: none; the repository's TLA+ modules, tools/tlacheck and the Makefile's tlc target. THE TASK (the DESIGN half). Extend tla/LandPass.tla so it models more than one base. Today the module has one base tree, so it cannot say that two streams on different bases are independent. Add a constant `Bases` and a map `baseOf[s]` (each stream's base branch; a stream's batch lands on its own base), make the base tree, the pushes ghost, the cut/chain, the landGrace wait and the gate's one-writer rule per base (a base commit's gate stays single-writer only per base commit; two bases have different commits), and add a ghost `waits` (the set of pairs (s,t) such that the lander made s wait for t: the cut chain, the grace wait, a gate slot, a width slot) recorded by every action that can block one stream on another. INVARIANT `DistinctBasesNeverOrdered`: for every pair (s,t) in `waits`, baseOf[s] = baseOf[t], except the width bound (BoundHeld, `running <= Width`), which is a capacity bound and is modelled as a counter, never as a pair: Width is derived from bench capacity (card sprint-spec-fix-land-width-from-bench) and must be at least 2, so add the constant assumption `Width >= 2` and a TypeOK line saying so. Two streams on different bases are never ordered by the lander. REVERSED WITNESS: Broken = "serialbases": the lander serializes landings (and the merges) through one global queue, as `--land-parallel 1` and a grace wait on a stream of another base do today; TLC must find a state where `waits` holds a pair with distinct bases, violating DistinctBasesNeverOrdered. Add tla/MCLandPassBrokenSerialBases.cfg (the witness) and tla/MCLandPassBases.cfg (the passing instance: two bases, three streams, Width 2, the same Touches and Heads shape as MCLandPass.cfg so it stays small). The existing MCLandPass*.cfg instances use one base (Bases = {b1}) and must keep their outcomes; the existing `inorder` witness (NoHeadOfLine) must still fail and NoHeadOfLine still hold: ordering by priority within one base must never hold up a green batch (landGrace on one base is the owner's 2026-10-10 compromise, and card sprint-spec-fix-land-grace-same-base removes the wait for a stream still merging; model that too: a built batch lands at once, so the grace action is gone and a `Broken = "gracewait"` witness makes the lander wait for a still-merging stream, violating NoHeadOfLine on one base AND DistinctBasesNeverOrdered on two). Record the model's names for the code cards in a comment block at the top of LandPass.tla ("R-LAND-PARALLEL"): the invariant `DistinctBasesNeverOrdered`, the witnesses `serialbases` and `gracewait`, and the action each Go function implements (launch, runLane, acquireGate, graceClock, the width semaphore). Update tla/COVERAGE.tsv's LandPass row (it already lists the module's invariants and witnesses; keep it one row) and tla/README.md; TLC runs on a bench only: follow the recipe (push the branch; on captain clone it and run `make tlc TLC_GROUP=<the LandPass group>`), merge the RUNS.tsv records with tools/tlacheck, and verify every counterexample against landpass.go by hand before writing it down. From: card moved out of the sprint (work record, 2026-10-19)

### defer takes a review, ready or failed card and keeps its head

defer takes only waiting cards. It cannot defer a review, ready or failed card while keeping its pushed head, and a held stream still deals reworked cards, so rework is no way to park one: on 2026-10-19 every stream deferred left its review and ready cards in the sprint.

Why it waits: Needs a design for what a deferred head is and how a resumed card picks it up.

From: found deferring the sprint's non-rocketnet cards, 2026-10-19

### defer's moved= count is the number of cards it wrote

defer --expect 37 printed moved=38 for sprint-spec while writing 37; the same day vg-rules --expect 1 printed moved=3, moo --expect 14 moved=15, framework-delta --expect 9 moved=10. The count seems to include the queue moves it prints as MOVED lines. moved= should be the cards deferred, and equal --expect.

From: found deferring the sprint's non-rocketnet cards, 2026-10-19

### A refused defer writes nothing to the roadmap

defer --stream vg-physics --expect 11 was REFUSED (vg-stone-colour-adopt is needed by vg-render-takes-vg-physics-placement; DEFER FAILED moved=0 refused=1) and deferred nothing in the store, yet it wrote all 11 cards' items into robotgamedevelopers/virtualgo docs/roadmap.sexp: the file and the store disagree, and a retry meets its own items. The roadmap write must follow the store's commit, or be undone with it.

From: found deferring the sprint's non-rocketnet cards, 2026-10-19

### defer adds the (group "sprint" ...) record when a roadmap has none

defer refuses a roadmap with no (group "sprint" ...) record, and nova-work roadmap check refuses a group that holds no item, so the group cannot be added on its own: on 2026-10-19 each repository needed a hand-written placeholder item, removed after the defer. defer should add the group in the same write, and create docs/roadmap.sexp when a repository has none.

### A card brought back into play on a held stream returns to waiting

On a held stream, a card that rework, a broken read verdict or add puts back into play goes to WAITING. It is never ready and never dealt. Unholding lets the next tick move it on. Observed 2026-10-19: reworked cards sat in ready forever on held stream rocketnet-tests (rocketnet-cbmc-ack-block-read, rocketnet-cbmc-server-packet-readers); a card reworked by a broken read after the hold of schema-c-cpp was dealt to friend.emma (cpp-carries-the-json-options w4); a card added to held stream schema-dart was dealt (schema-dart-runs-hostile-corpus-t w1). Tests: one per path (rework, broken read verdict, add), each on a held stream, with time as an argument; plus an invariant that no card is in ready on a held stream after any step.

Why it waits: Ready lasts at most one tick before the deal; a held stream must not strand or deal cards

From: the owner, 2026-10-19

### Throughput counts only cards that landed

Throughput (cards per hour on the dashboard and in where) counts only cards that landed in the window. A card that is archived, deferred to a roadmap, dropped or moved out must never count. Observed 2026-10-19: 302 cards/hour shown during a bulk move of about 600 cards to roadmaps. Code location: the dashboard's rate is pageThroughput.add in internal/sprintdash/pageview.go (and sample_landed in internal/sprintdash/stopgap/server.py), which takes cards an hour from the change in the sampled landed count over the samples' span, so any move that raises that count is counted as a landing; where's own landing rate is in internal/sprint/rate.go (LandingRate). Tests: a window with N landings and M archives, defers and drops reports N per window, with time as an argument.

Why it waits: A rate that counts bulk moves reads far above the real landing rate and hides how fast work lands

Target: v1.7

From: the owner, 2026-10-19

### The lander checks soft dependencies before it pushes

The lander must check a card's LAND-AFTER (soft) dependencies before the merge and the push, never after. Observed 2026-10-19 at 12:23: the lander pushed luau-fix-node-index-shift to sprint/schema-luau at 07f5155, and only then refused to report because its LAND-AFTER dependency luau-fix-root-trailing-bytes had not landed. The base held B before A, against the declared order. Fix: evaluate soft dependencies first; a card whose soft dependency is unlanded is skipped this batch with nothing merged or pushed. Test: B is queued with A unlanded; nothing is pushed and B is skipped this batch.

Why it waits: A push before the dependency check puts the base in an order the cards declared against

Target: v1.7

From: the owner, 2026-10-19

### A repository declares its own generated ledgers for the lander

The lander's generated-ledger list is hard-coded in var landLedgers in cmd/nova-sprint/landledger.go (lines 52-79), so a repo cannot declare its own, and a pin file every card re-pins makes every concurrent card conflict. Observed 2026-10-19: schema-java's internal/codegen/javatable/testdata/keyedindex_base.sha256 forced 5+ reworks, each costing two new reads. Proposal: a repo file .nova/ledgers.sexp gives paths, owning tests and an update command, appended in ledgers(). Safety: regenerate only when BOTH sides of the merge re-pinned the file, otherwise refuse; the pin guards intentional wire moves, so it must never be silently accepted. The schema-java entry: SCHEMA_UPDATE_KEYED_GOLDEN=1 go test -count=1 -run '^TestKeyedFormLeavesWireCodeByteIdentical$' ./internal/codegen/javatable

Why it waits: Without a repo-declared ledger, one re-pinned file makes every concurrent card conflict and rework

Target: v1.7

From: the owner, 2026-10-19

### The lander does not read a merge card before the accept has drained

After accept, the merge card is Queued at once (internal/sprint/steps_review.go:1384), but the primary's move to merging, with readers and heavy_*, waits for the next tick's drain (store/engine.go:787, sprint.QueueOf, queue.go:44). If the land loop reads in that gap, readsWhy (cmd/nova-sprint/land.go:736-742, via ReadsStanding readers.go:407) counts 0 of 2 readers and logs a refusal. Harmless, because the card lands on the next cycle, but misleading. Observed 2026-10-19 on rocketnet-iocp-live-matrix-speed: refused at 13:43:56, landed at 13:44:43. Fix: skip a queued merge card whose primary is not yet in Merging and say 'accept not drained yet', or load with the work queue applied. Model the split write (accept queues the merge card, the drain moves the primary) in tla/Land.tla, with a witness for the race.

Why it waits: A refusal logged in the gap between accept and the next drain is misleading, though harmless

Target: v1.7

From: the owner, 2026-10-19

### Landing and stitching run continuously and in parallel per area, never one card at a time and never left to the end

Observed 2026-10-21: the sprint left ~3,960 schema branches and streams hundreds of commits apart (dart 1,328 behind main), virtualgo with ~200 unlanded branches, moo's layers 3-5 only on sprint/moo; a live session then consolidated virtualgo, moo and schema's Go core in hours with parallel per-area land lanes (land/<lane> from main, merge the stream, resolve against the spec, one coordinator merging in order). Glenn: "nothing says the merging or coordination and stitching together has to be done one card at a time, in fact, the intent that it is not!" Proposal: (1) a standing integration worker per area folds that area's gated cards onto main continuously, in batches of whatever is ready, gate once on the batch; no card waits on a stream branch. (2) A hard drift limit: no stream more than N commits or H hours from main; past it the sprint stops dealing new cards into that stream and deals an integrate-this-stream card at frontier tier instead (mechanical, like the other gates). (3) The landing rules become sprint law: main's newer decisions win; carry the stream's intent onto main, never revert main to fit; one version of each thing. (4) Superseded detection as a tool: contained / same patch-id / identical tree / squash-landed classify most branches mechanically (the 2026-10-21 scripts), only the remainder go to a worker; attempt branches are deleted once their card's landing decision is made. (5) Core-first fan-out is generated: when a core change lands with a spec delta (schema's Go core), the sprint deals one adopt-the-spec-delta card per dependent lane. (6) Main stays green: a cross-lane merge order, a TLA+ model of the landing train with reversed witnesses (a lane landing red, a stream past its drift limit, a card that never reaches main). Per the v1.9 method these become owner-dictated situation-to-expectation cases locked as tests, e.g. a stream 200 commits behind main: no new cards dealt to it; an integrate card appears.

Why it waits: Cards that never reach main are not progress; the 2026-10-21 cleanup cost a day and showed parallel per-area landing works

### Goal cards, live steering, context packs and proportionate review: what the sprint learns from coordinator sessions

Observed 2026-10-21: a live coordinator session working through child agents landed virtualgo, moo and schema's Go core in hours, where the sprint had scattered ~3,960 schema branches. Glenn: "we want to do both ... improve sprint with lessons learned from outside it." Companion to continuous-parallel-landing. (1) GOAL CARDS: a card may carry an outcome and an area (land stream X onto main; make port Y pass the spec delta; make the stone tink audible) and the worker plans its own steps inside fixed rails (drift limit, gates, landing law, one version of each thing), instead of only pre-cut cards with fixed PATHS. (2) LIVE STEERING: a ruling channel per card: the owner's new direction (e.g. portable first; time not counts) reaches running cards as an append-only note over the bus within a minute, recorded once and pushed to every affected card, without bouncing the card the way a brief edit does today. (3) CONTEXT PACKS: each card gets a generated pack of the owner's relevant rulings, spec deltas and neighbouring lanes' state, refreshed when they change, instead of only what the card writer typed. (4) PROPORTIONATE REVIEW: one cold read or a strong-model spot check of the claims that matter (hashes, CI, file lists, determinism) for most cards; full multi-reader reads only for high-blast changes; landing evidence (CI, TLC, hash re-pins with reasons) counts as part of the read. (5) Keep the sprint's strengths that sessions lack: model tiers, fleet scheduling with per-machine widths, durable leases surviving crashes, dashboards. As v1.9 behaviour these become owner-dictated situation-to-expectation cases locked as tests, e.g. the owner issues a ruling while 3 cards in that area are working: each receives it within a minute and none is bounced.

Why it waits: Goal-shaped work, live steering and lean review made the session fast; the sprint should have them without losing its durability and cheap tiers

### A plain finish whose report's verdict is not LAND or done is refused

nova-sprint finish without --failed records the attempt ok and sends it to a reader even when its --report text's verdict line is HOLD or not-done. finish refuses a plain finish whose report's verdict line is anything but LAND or done, naming the line and the --failed finish to run instead.

Why it waits: On one row 17 of 53 failed attempts were HOLD reports finished plain: each spent a read to learn what the report already said.

Target: v1.7

From: coordinator review 2026-10-24

### A broken read must name a defect class

A broken read whose finding names no defect is accepted and reworks the card. read --broken requires a defect class (DONE-WHEN unmet, PATHS, ledger, banned word, name, gate evidence, behaviour) beside the finding, and refuses without one.

Why it waits: A rework from a finding with no defect gives the worker nothing to fix, and the failure cannot be classified when a row's ok% falls.

Target: v1.7

From: coordinator review 2026-10-24

### One broken read no longer outvotes several ok reads

One broken read outvotes several ok reads at the same head, including a stale read against PATHS that were already amended in place. A broken read whose finding is answered by the card's current brief (amended PATHS or DONE-WHEN) is retired as stale, and a single broken read against several oks asks one more read instead of reworking.

Why it waits: Good heads were reworked on one stale or lone finding, spending a full attempt and its reads on work that was already right.

Target: v1.7

From: coordinator review 2026-10-24

### Fleet reads never launch without a route

Fleet read cards launch with no route and return no verdict, again and again for the same card. The deal refuses a read to a member with no route for the card's tier, and a read that returns with no verdict for want of a route is not dealt to that member again until its route is set.

Why it waits: Reads that cannot run hold cards in review past their deadlines and stall the row's landings.

Target: v1.7

From: coordinator review 2026-10-24

### Widening PATHS or DONE-WHEN in place does not re-deal the same head

Widening a card's PATHS or DONE-WHEN in place re-deals the work and re-reads the same unchanged head. An in-place widening that the current head already meets sends that head to review once at the new brief, without a new work attempt; a head a reader already found broken is never resent unchanged.

Why it waits: A widening meant to unblock a card spends another work attempt and its reads on a head that has not changed.

Target: v1.7

From: coordinator review 2026-10-24

### A pinned card taken back with friend take can be given again without a rebrief

A card whose WHO line pins one friend, taken back from that friend with friend take, waits out of the deal, as friend take's help says, but friend give did not hand it back either, so only a rebrief moved it. friend give hands a taken-back pinned card to the pinned friend, or to another named friend, without a rebrief, and the inbox names each pinned card that waits.

Why it waits: Pinned cards taken back sat out of the deal until the seat noticed them and rebriefed each one by hand.

Target: v1.7

From: coordinator review 2026-10-24

### A staged job directory never carries another card's RESULT.md or HEAD

A staged job directory can carry another card's RESULT.md and HEAD, so a worker can finish one card with another's report or head. Staging starts from a clean directory, checks that the staged HEAD is the card's BASE or carried head, and refuses a directory holding a report file for another card.

Why it waits: A finish built on another card's report or head is wrong in a way no reader of the brief expects, and wastes the attempt.

Target: v1.7

From: coordinator review 2026-10-24

### friend stage of a read card stages the exact head under read, read-only

nova-sprint friend stage of a read card fails. For a read with no NEXT it stages an empty checkout at main (git exits 128); for a carried card it stages the carried head instead of the head under read; and it writes no JOB.md. A read stages the exact head under read, read-only, with its JOB.md.

Why it waits: A reader staged at the wrong head reads the wrong work, or cannot read at all, so the read returns no verdict or a wrong one.

Target: v1.7

From: the coordinator, 2026-10-16

### One app starts at login and runs every nova service on the machine, configured from the friend list, never a launch agent per friend or job

After the 2026-10-16 reboot the studio had 45 files in ~/Library/LaunchAgents and more in /Library/LaunchDaemons, a plist for each friend hook (aurora, emma, johnny, stella), each friend runner, each loop, the dashboards, the redis instances and the sprint server. 19 were stale: editor backups, before-* and moved-to-* copies, a duplicate Stella hook, and sprint-table-live, which had crash-looped 23,923 times on a retired verb. Two more broke on the reboot because their paths pointed at a versioned Homebrew Cellar node and at /tmp. Each friend added, moved or retired meant a hand-written plist, and nothing removed the old one. The fix is one supervisor, installed as the only nova launch agent on a machine (plus one daemon only where root is needed, such as the CI runners). It reads which friends live on this machine, their harness, dirs and sessions from nova-config, and the machine's roles (store, sprint server, dashboard, hook-serve, loops) from the same config. It starts each child, restarts it with backoff, writes one log per child, and reports per-child state so nova-doctor shows a crash loop at once. Adding or moving a friend is a config change: the supervisor starts or stops her children, and a retired job disappears because config is the only source. It refuses a path under /tmp or a versioned Cellar path, and nova-doctor flags any other nova plist on the machine as a stray. The supervisor's states (absent, starting, running, backing-off, stopped, removed) get a TLA+ model before code, and unit tests use a fake clock and a fake process starter. Covers nova-tools binaries too (nova-hook, nova-friend, nova-swarm loops, nova-secrets exec wrappers), and the fleet's ansible plays install only the supervisor.

Why it waits: A launch agent per friend and per job grew to dozens of plists that nobody removed, and stale ones broke things and loaded the machine (Glenn, 2026-10-16).

Target: v1.7

From: Glenn, live, 2026-10-16: 'consolidate all these things into one app that starts at startup and has configuration according to friends, not an app per-friend'

### nova-sprint log honours --max and names the rest

Repository mas-bandwidth/nova-sprint. Extends nova-sprint log (cmd/nova-sprint/log.go), never a second mechanism. Problem: `nova-sprint log --since 1h --max 5` printed 2,985 entries, ending `LOG OK lines=2985 of=127415` (854 KB). log.go never reads c.max, and log.go:120 prints every line. Smallest fix: honour --max with a default of 20, end a cut list with `MORE kind=log shown=<n> total=<t> run: nova-sprint log <same filters> --max 0`, and add --grep and --kind later if needed. The help text is corrected by the v1.4.x text fix (the store-verbs --max paragraph now says log does not cap yet); this is the behaviour, and the fix reverses that paragraph when it lands. Tool: nova-sprint log. Tests are unit tests: no real time, no sockets, no network.

Why it waits: A bounded look at the log cost 854 KB because --max is parsed and ignored.

### CI pause, part 1 of 3 (nova-sprint): fleet quiet --ci pauses a machine's runners for a bounded window, with the model

Repository mas-bandwidth/nova-sprint, tier heavy. Extends fleet quiet (cmd/nova-sprint/fleetquiet.go; rule internal/sprint/fleet_quiet.go: Quiet, quietPlan, quietEnds, QuietLines), never a second mechanism: Quiet gains ci, FleetReq (internal/sprint/steps_work.go) carries it, the queue answer gains ci_pause (cmd/nova-sprint/view.go), fleet beat gains --runners (cmd/nova-sprint/fleet.go, stored in internal/sprint/presence.go), where gains the ci cell (cmd/nova-sprint/reads.go); docs/SPEC-SPRINT.md section fleet-quiet-machine-b.w7 and docs/CLI.md follow. THE MODEL, written first: tla/RunnerPause.tla (clock, pause, per runner state, job, interrupted; actions Tick, SetPause with until <= clock + Cap, EndPause, JobStart, JobEnd, GateStep, and RaceAssign, the accepted race of a job assigned between the gate's read and its SIGINT). Properties NeverSignalBusy, BoundedPause, PausedOnlyWhilePaused and the liveness ResumesAfterDeadline. Three reversed witnesses: MCRunnerPauseBrokenKillBusy fails NeverSignalBusy, MCRunnerPauseBrokenNoExpiry fails ResumesAfterDeadline, MCRunnerPauseBrokenNoCap fails BoundedPause; group runnerpause in tla/CASES.tsv, TLC on a Linux bench, records merged with tlacheck merge --keep. Tests: internal/sprint TestFleetQuietCIPausesAndEndsAtItsTime, cmd/nova-sprint TestFleetQuietCIVerbQueueBeatAndWhere. THE CONTRACT, shared by the three CI-pause entries (ci-pause-sprint-record, ci-pause-runner-gate, ci-pause-member-carrier): (1) Record: fleet quiet <m> (--for|--until) --reason <text> --ci sets the member's quiet with ci true; the deal effect is the quiet's as today; a CI quiet more than 24h from now is refused, nothing written, naming the cap (CIQuietMost); --end and the tick's quietEnds end the CI pause with the quiet; the QUIET line of a CI quiet ends '; CI paused'. (2) Carrier: queue --as <m> --json carries ci_pause {until RFC3339 UTC, until_unix, reason} while the asking member's CI quiet is active, and no ci_pause key otherwise. (3) Pause file: the member writes it atomically (temp file in the same directory, then rename) as {until, until_unix, set_unix, reason} while ci_pause is present and removes it when absent; its path is the runner unit's NOVA_CI_PAUSE_FILE: linux the seat's $HOME/nova-bench/runners/ci-pause.json, darwin /Users/Shared/nova-runners/ci-pause.json (mode 2775, group staff: the darwin runner seat is a separate account). (4) Gate, per runner, FAIL OPEN: a pause is active iff the file parses, now < until_unix and until_unix <= set_unix + 86400; absent, unreadable, past or over the cap is no pause, CI on, so a dead sprint or member can never leave CI off. States: enabled -> draining (pause active, the runner's Runner.Worker is running a job) -> paused (child stopped by SIGINT) -> enabled (pause not active: child started again); enabled goes straight to paused when idle; draining goes back to enabled with no signal when the pause lifts first. DRAIN, NEVER KILL: the gate never signals a child whose Runner.Worker is running. It polls every NOVA_GATE_EVERY seconds (default 15). (5) Gate report: <pause dir>/state/<runner name>.json {state, at_unix} on each change. (6) Beat and view: the member sends fleet beat <m> --runners enabled=<n>,draining=<n>,paused=<n>,unmanaged=<n> (unmanaged: a Runner.Listener with no state file, e.g. one started from a shell outside its unit) only when the installed fleet beat -h lists --runners; the beat stores the counts beside no_room and refuses a malformed word naming the form; where and where --all show one cell per fleet member: ci=on, ci=paused until <time>, ci=draining <n>, ci=unmanaged <n> (the remedy is a converge of that host's runners), ci=- with no counts; where --json carries the same. Unit tests use no real time (clocks start at 1000 seconds), no sockets, no network: fakes for the store, the server, the process table and the files; real runner control is functional-tier only, and converging the fleet stays the coordinator's act.

Why it waits: fleet quiet and fleet hold stop sprint deals only; nothing pauses a machine's GitHub Actions runners, and a quiet window on amd-1 on 2026-10-16 was made by stopping its runners by hand. A pause must let running jobs finish, can never stay on past its deadline, and shows in the sprint's views.

Target: v1.7

### CI pause, part 3 of 3 (nova-tools): the member writes the pause file from its queue answer and reports its runners on the beat

Repository mas-bandwidth/nova-tools, tier pro. Extends nova-swarm member (pkg/member/member.go: Member.Beat, queueOut, noRoomArgs and drainArgs; cmd/nova-swarm/member.go: probeLoadUnmeasured, the pattern for probing --runners), never a second mechanism: new pkg/member/cipause.go keeps the pause file matching ci_pause per (3) (set_unix kept while until_unix is unchanged, nothing written when it already matches, a failed write one NOTE and a retry), reads the state directory and the process table (a seam) for the counts of (6), and Beat appends --runners only when the probe lists it; cmd/nova-swarm/member.go adds --ci-pause-file (default by OS per (3)); docs/CLI.md and docs/SPEC-SWARM.md follow. It lands safely before the other two parts: with no ci_pause key and no --runners in the help it writes and sends nothing extra. Tests: pkg/member TestCIPauseFileFollowsTheQueue, TestCIPauseBeatReportsRunners. THE CONTRACT, shared by the three CI-pause entries (ci-pause-sprint-record, ci-pause-runner-gate, ci-pause-member-carrier): (1) Record: fleet quiet <m> (--for|--until) --reason <text> --ci sets the member's quiet with ci true; the deal effect is the quiet's as today; a CI quiet more than 24h from now is refused, nothing written, naming the cap (CIQuietMost); --end and the tick's quietEnds end the CI pause with the quiet; the QUIET line of a CI quiet ends '; CI paused'. (2) Carrier: queue --as <m> --json carries ci_pause {until RFC3339 UTC, until_unix, reason} while the asking member's CI quiet is active, and no ci_pause key otherwise. (3) Pause file: the member writes it atomically (temp file in the same directory, then rename) as {until, until_unix, set_unix, reason} while ci_pause is present and removes it when absent; its path is the runner unit's NOVA_CI_PAUSE_FILE: linux the seat's $HOME/nova-bench/runners/ci-pause.json, darwin /Users/Shared/nova-runners/ci-pause.json (mode 2775, group staff: the darwin runner seat is a separate account). (4) Gate, per runner, FAIL OPEN: a pause is active iff the file parses, now < until_unix and until_unix <= set_unix + 86400; absent, unreadable, past or over the cap is no pause, CI on, so a dead sprint or member can never leave CI off. States: enabled -> draining (pause active, the runner's Runner.Worker is running a job) -> paused (child stopped by SIGINT) -> enabled (pause not active: child started again); enabled goes straight to paused when idle; draining goes back to enabled with no signal when the pause lifts first. DRAIN, NEVER KILL: the gate never signals a child whose Runner.Worker is running. It polls every NOVA_GATE_EVERY seconds (default 15). (5) Gate report: <pause dir>/state/<runner name>.json {state, at_unix} on each change. (6) Beat and view: the member sends fleet beat <m> --runners enabled=<n>,draining=<n>,paused=<n>,unmanaged=<n> (unmanaged: a Runner.Listener with no state file, e.g. one started from a shell outside its unit) only when the installed fleet beat -h lists --runners; the beat stores the counts beside no_room and refuses a malformed word naming the form; where and where --all show one cell per fleet member: ci=on, ci=paused until <time>, ci=draining <n>, ci=unmanaged <n> (the remedy is a converge of that host's runners), ci=- with no counts; where --json carries the same. Unit tests use no real time (clocks start at 1000 seconds), no sockets, no network: fakes for the store, the server, the process table and the files; real runner control is functional-tier only, and converging the fleet stays the coordinator's act.

Why it waits: fleet quiet and fleet hold stop sprint deals only; nothing pauses a machine's GitHub Actions runners, and a quiet window on amd-1 on 2026-10-16 was made by stopping its runners by hand. A pause must let running jobs finish, can never stay on past its deadline, and shows in the sprint's views.

Target: v1.7
